issues.problem: rules[8] example pinyin wrote 一个 as 'yī gè'; 个 is neutral here and the rest of the guide writes 'ge'.
rules[4] glossed 精 as 'fine, lively', which is vague and does not fit the drilled word 精彩.
The hsk4-words sub-point lists '必需 for 必须 before a verb' as an error, but the rules never said that 必需 is a real word (必需品). If applied mechanically, a learner could mark every 必需 wrong.
issues.action: Added to rules[11].note that 必需 exists but 'must' before a verb is 必须.

issues.problem: 既 / 即 was covered only by an origin story, with no visible shape cue for telling them apart.
issues.action: Rewrote rules[11].note to give 既 ends in 旡, 即 ends in 卩, alongside the mnemonic, and kept it within the 300-character limit.
